Chinese premier chairs State Council executive meeting

Updated: October 23, 2026 21:30 Xinhua [![](/static/2023GW/images/Artical_Print.jpg)](javascript:window.print\(\))

BEIJING, Oct. 23 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Friday presided over a State Council executive meeting that studied measures to coordinate population development with economic and social development and heard a report on the implementation of the arrangements made at the national conference on the services sector.

Noting that population is fundamental to a country's economic and social development, the meeting called for efforts to tap the demographic dividend and support high-quality economic and social development through high-quality population development.

The meeting stressed the need to expand skills training and better align education and training with industrial development to promote high-quality and full employment.

It also called for steady progress in ensuring equal access to basic public services and optimizing the infrastructure layout in line with population distribution.

Efforts should be made to accelerate the development of a birth-friendly society and to maintain a stable number of newborns, according to the meeting.

Regarding the service industry, the meeting emphasized its underpinning role in driving economic growth and called for stronger support in areas such as financing, land use, talent and data.

The meeting urged continuous efforts to break down market access barriers, remove hidden hurdles for private investment, and explore innovative development paths tailored to local conditions.

It also emphasized the need to increase investment in the services sector to unleash the potential of service consumption as well as cultivate leading enterprises and distinctive brands.

China issues guidelines for reinforcing integration of sci-tech, industrial innovations

Updated: October 22, 2026 20:20 Xinhua [![](/static/2023GW/images/Artical_Print.jpg)](javascript:window.print\(\))

BEIJING, Oct. 22 -- China has released a set of guidelines on promoting the deep integration of scientific and technological innovation and industrial innovation.

Issued by the General Office of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council, this document provides a comprehensive blueprint for advancing the deep integration of sci-tech and industrial innovations.

It requires efforts to deepen the implementation of the innovation-driven development strategy, with the goals of developing new quality productive forces and building a modern industrial system, and with a focus on establishing an enterprise-led, multi-stakeholder collaborative system for integrated industry-academia-research innovation, so as to form a new pattern in which sci-tech innovation and industrial innovation promote each other.

This document is of great significance for accelerating high-level sci-tech self-reliance and strength, cultivating and developing new quality productive forces, building China into a competitive sci-tech country, and realizing Chinese modernization, said an official with the Ministry of Science and Technology.

It highlights the necessity to stimulate vitality via reform, requiring that sci-tech innovation should be strengthened with an application-oriented approach while industrial development should clearly define its sci-tech innovation tasks.

The document specifies concrete measures in six areas, namely seamlessly connecting the innovation chain with the industrial chain, supporting the building of a modern industrial system with the supply of high-quality sci-tech achievements, strengthening enterprise-led industry-academia-research collaborative innovation, improving the efficiency of coordinated allocation of innovation resources, fostering a sound ecosystem, and expanding the space for deep integration.

The official noted that the translation of sci-tech achievements into practical productive forces is manifested in spawning new industries and driving industrial transformation. Therefore, it is necessary to promptly apply innovation achievements to industries and industrial chains.

The document puts forward three measures in this regard: enhancing the self-reliance and controllability of industrial chains through breakthroughs in key technologies, cultivating and expanding emerging industries and future industries via original and disruptive sci-tech innovation, and transforming and upgrading traditional industries through the application of advanced technologies.

The official underlined the significance of strengthening enterprises' principal role in innovation. The document outlines three measures regarding this aim, which are enhancing corporate innovation capabilities, accelerating the development of sci-tech enterprises, and promoting greater synergy among innovators.

To improve the allocation of innovation resources, it stipulates measures to foster a virtuous cycle among science, industry and finance, enhance coordinated talent development and utilization, and build integrated innovation platforms.

China issues guidelines to promote employment amid AI advances

Updated: October 23, 2026 20:08 Xinhua [![](/static/2023GW/images/Artical_Print.jpg)](javascript:window.print\(\))

BEIJING, Oct. 23 -- China has rolled out guidelines on adapting to advances in artificial intelligence (AI) to promote employment-friendly development, aiming to harness the technology to create jobs, improve employment quality and stimulate entrepreneurship while mitigating job displacement caused by AI applications.

The guidelines, issued by the General Office of the State Council, set out 18 tasks in six areas, including boosting AI's job-creation potential, making AI adoption more employment-friendly, improving workers' digital skills, enhancing employment services, strengthening labor and social security protections, and monitoring and addressing employment risks.

The guidelines call for expanding employment opportunities in emerging fields, helping micro, small and medium-sized enterprises stabilize and expand employment, fostering new forms of employment and entrepreneurship in the AI sector, and developing new AI-related occupations.

The guidelines urge efforts to tap AI's job-creation potential in traditional sectors, mitigate job displacement caused by AI applications, and establish a mechanism to assess employment risks associated with AI adoption.

The guidelines emphasize improving the framework for protecting workers' rights in human-machine collaboration, strengthening social security for people in flexible employment and those in new forms of employment, and refining income distribution mechanisms to adapt to advances in AI.
